outputs.headline: False: Hot lemon water does not destroy coronavirus
outputs.summary: Drinking hot water with lemon juice does not prevent or cure COVID-19, according to health experts and fact-checking organizations.
outputs.what_post_claims: The post claims that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice will destroy the coronavirus.
outputs.what_is_true: Health experts and fact-checking organizations have confirmed that drinking hot water with lemon juice does not prevent or cure COVID-19. This is a widely debunked myth from the early pandemic.
evidence_against: AFP reported in March 2020 that claims about warm water with lemon preventing coronavirus are false.
AP News stated in April 2020 that hot water, lemon, and baking soda will not cure coronavirus.
Hackensack Meridian Health confirmed that home remedies, including warm water or lemon juice, are not effective against COVID-19.
outputs.sources_spoken: AFP, AP News, and Hackensack Meridian Health
outputs.audio_script: A social media post claims that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice will destroy the coronavirus. This is false.
